utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue. Is the witness here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Before the witness comes in, I just have two -- three matters to raise which will take four or five minutes. The first relates to an application pursuant to Rule 73 to vary the Prosecution's exhibit list. The witness who will be testifying this afternoon, when I met her yesterday for proofing, brought with her some DVD, two DVDs, with excerpts of news footage; one from German television and one from the Bosnian television studios. I have disclosed them to Defence yesterday and I have asked the Defence -- I have basically explained to the Defence that I would use them in examination of the witness, and I understand they have no objection to that. But officially I have to seek your leave to vary the exhibit list, put them on the exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think it's more than officially; you have to show good cause. But we'll consider it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we grant it. We grant the application.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The second issue relates to Witness 66, who is testifying tomorrow, and it's essentially a minor application pursuant to Rule 75; that is, when I ask him about his current employment, he would ask that that be done in private session; in other words, just one question, because his current employment involves travel to Republika Srpska, and for that one question he ask that be done in private session. Again, I mentioned this to Defence counsel and they have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. We grant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the third minor matter is with respect to Exhibit P00256. I understand that there was a MFI -- actually, it hasn't been admitted because there was a translation pending. I have been informed that a translation is now available and therefore I seek to move that MFI into evidence, as an exhibit, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Have we seen the translation? It's P00256. Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And your turn now, Mr. Waespi, with the witness to continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In fact, it's a new witness; it's W-50. Pursuant to your oral ruling of yesterday, the person has image distortion and also a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you may begin, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you feel okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown a piece of paper with her name on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that this is your name on this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If that could be tendered under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P289, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the exhibit -- ter number 02988 could be prepared, please, to be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I will be referring to a witness number this afternoon. I will not mention your name, but I will be referring to you as Witness W-50.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, if you look at this screen - and that should not be broadcast, please - do you remember that you gave a witness statement to investigators of the Tribunal on the 16th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: The 16th? Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember that I showed you this statement yesterday in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I remember that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember that you told me you would like to make two corrections in this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the first correction relates to the second page - I think that is the only page, substantive page, in this statement - and it's the second line of the second page, and it says: "I am from Foca originally." Can you tell Their Honours where you were from originally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Originally, I'm from Masline, a village that is part of Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Witness. The second clarification relates to a sentence in the third paragraph, and I'll quote the English version: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What is the comment or correction or clarification you would like to make in relation to this sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: There is one thing I'd like to clarify. I'm not sure about this, whether it came from the left side or the right side, east or west. One thing I do know for certain is that the shot came from Zecija Glava, from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I think you will be able to show us on a photo where -- the direction the shots were fired from was, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I hope that I will be able to help you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Now, with these two corrections or clarifications, is this witness statement a true and accurate record of what had happened on that day, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And if you were to answer the same questions today, would these answers be the same as recorded in your statement of November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Indeed, they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, if this statement could be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P290, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember the weather on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, not really. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, what were you doing on that morning, on that day? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you carry canisters with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how did you carry the canisters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: We used a length of rope.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you carry the canisters in your hands or over your shoulders or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: My shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Were your hands free or did you hold something else in your hands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: My hands were free.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how was she hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Because the bullet had come from Zecija Glava, she was hit in her left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What did you do after she was hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I called her to come behind a holiday cottage that was there, and I administered first aid to her right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what were her injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Serious ones. She was bleeding profusely and I helped as much as I could, on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And on which body parts were her injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: On her arm, the fist specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know which arm it was, left or right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: The left one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And was there only one shot or were there several shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: There were two shots at the time, the time she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And at whom were these shots directed to, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If a video could be played. This is ter number 02717. And the last exhibit should also be tendered under seal because the statement carries the witness's name. It should be played in private session, though, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could you please ask the witness to show again which fist was hit, because it looked to me on the video clip as if she was pointing to her right hand and I think she just said it was her left hand. So which was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: It was the left hand, the fist. What I showed in that video clip was me trying to show which way she was facing when the bullet hit her, and that's why I used that hand. So I tried to use my own hand -- my right hand when I was showing that, but as a matter of fact the wound that she received was to her left fist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, and thank you, Your Honours. I would like to show you two or three photos taken from that video, and we'll start with --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to tender this video under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P291, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown ter number 02993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you see a photo on your screen, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell us the direction of the house where you were departing that morning? And perhaps you could mark it with the help of the usher.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I don't understand your question. Can you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Can we see the house you were leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. Behind this house, the one behind this one. You can't actually see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you for the marking. Can you attach a letter to your mark, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. So that morning, you were using that path to come down to the bigger road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, the path.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we could move to the next picture; this is 02990. And this exhibit, this photo, should be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you see another photo on the screen, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And please attach a letter A to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And can you indicate the direction you wanted to walk towards the water point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Sure. We were supposed to cross this road right here where she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And would you go left or right? Would you go past the red car or would you go to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Where the police officer is standing, the red car. We were supposed to walk past them and then continue in this same direction down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you take her to a doctor or a hospital thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I first took her to see the nearest doctor who then helped her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how far away was the nearest doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: It's difficult to say with any degree of precision, but it was quite far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And in relation to this house here, was it on the right side or on the left side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question. What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I apologise. You said you went to see the doctor and it was quite far away. Into which direction did you have to walk from this point, to the right side or to the left side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: To the left, this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you indicate with a cross, perhaps, the direction you were walking to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could add the letter D to the cross, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If this photo could also be tendered as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor, excuse me, before we remove this picture from the screen. Witness, you have told us that the shooting came from the direction you indicated with a C on the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is as follows: How did you come to that conclusion? Is it because you heard the shot, or did you hear the bullet whistle past, or is it because the police told you after the incident, or the investigators, after the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bullet came and we clearly heard it flying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the whistle or the actual bang?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yeah, I was referring to this whizzing or whistle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because when I was taking her to the doctor from this weekend cottage, while we were walking together, although I know nothing about weapons, there was firing. You could hear the sound of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Mindua. Mr. President, I know I'm beyond the 15 minutes allotted for this witness. With your leave, I would like to show just one document to this witness. It will take no longer than two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could show ter number 00894, an investigative file, to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you remember that I have shown you this document in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to go through it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I had the chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If we can go to page number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the page on the right side, the B/C/S is the right, but the page on the left side should be two pages earlier. The English translation should be two pages beforehand. No, it's the next page. On the left side of -- yes, that's it, that's the corresponding translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How many pages are we speaking about altogether?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Seven pages, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and thanks for the understanding of taking a little bit more time. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, you're being asked by the interpreter to repeat the numbers of the different documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So P294 and 65 ter 894. I'm waiting for this document so as to orient my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you good at reading maps? Are you able to orient yourself on the Sarajevo street map, Witness? Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Can you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I need to organise myself and organise my cross-examination today, so my question to you is as follows: Are you able to comment on a Sarajevo street map with your neighbourhood, with your area on the street plan? You know, these are tourist maps. Are you able to read that? Did you think this is possible or not at all? Maybe we'll give it a try later on, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The proof of the pudding is in the eating. Put it to her and see what happens.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same report as the one we've just seen. Can we turn to page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was this on the 11th of March, 1995? Was that the date when you went to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you read the signature that is on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's what is written by hand. It's not typewritten. It's written by hand with a pen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, but somebody else signed on her behalf because she is illiterate. And she maybe could have left her thumb print instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi is on his feet. Let's hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, if we could make a redaction in the -- it's on line 18 -- line 14 and 15, page 18, before it goes out, because that's obviously a protected witness. Just to make sure that we don't broadcast these statements. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I think you got the answer you deserve.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness - not Your Honour, but Witness - did you see the person who signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, I didn't really.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Were other civilians there with you, notwithstanding policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: [No verbal response].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I shall now ask you a number of questions concerning your statement. You will remember that a few minutes ago you addressed a number of matters with the Prosecution, a statement made on the 16th of November, 1995. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember another statement, in other words, another interview you had with the representatives from the OTP on the 4th of October, 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Well, in 2002? No, I don't remember that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: A few minutes ago you made two changes to your statement. The second change or correction you made, do you remember that, or do we need to see it on the screen again? Would you like us to display your statement on the screen again, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: If possible, I'd like to see it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the second page of the statement on the screen, please. Let's move straight to the second page. To avoid -- this cannot be broadcast. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You made a second change, as you can see, and the second change had to do with the direction of fire. Do you remember that? In your statement it is said: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I remember that, but the correction -- since I didn't know anything, I wasn't a local there, and I was afraid, that's why I said it. The only thing I know is that the bullet came precisely from Zecija Glava, although I am not an expert in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to check is the following: You mentioned that the shot came from the west. Is that what you said on the 16th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, at the time when you made your statement, did somebody suggest to you that the shot came from the west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, nobody suggested that because no one was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So why did you mention it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I just said it because I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't know. I was confused.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Witness, this is the truth: This is not where the shot came from. It did not come from the west?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think this is unfair towards the witness. I think she indicated clearly already in chief, and now again, that she is not sure what east and west is, but she states unequivocally that it came from Zecija Glava, whether that's east or west. I think that's adequately explained by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see nothing unreasonable in the line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, are you sure, then, that it came from Zecija Glava; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I'm 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Between Zecija Glava and the spot you have shown us on the photograph and which we will see again, what distance was there between these two locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Well, I didn't measure the distance. I'm not an expert in these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the first line," what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Serbian positions, from which the bullet came. That's what the first line is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when you say talk about "the first line," what do you compare it with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know whether there was another line held by the ABiH army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Well, there was the Serbian army and the army, holding the same positions and fighting each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What you have in mind are two armies that were pitched one against the other in the city centre and in the area surrounding Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: First, there was the Serbian army, holding the positions from which the shot came. I meant that place specifically. I was not referring to other places that you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time where the ABiH army soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. I wasn't a soldier; I was simply a civilian. And I didn't know where they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: How did you get to know that the soldiers of the Republika Srpska were at Zecija Glava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Well, I knew it. They were shooting every day, firing shells and using other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Were you sure that this was the army of the Republika Srpska at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I just told you that I was sure, and I tell you again that I'm sure that it came from this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we are not discussing the direction this shot came from for the time being. But at Zecija Glava, did you have an opportunity to see soldiers from the Republika Srpska? That was the question I asked you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I couldn't see. I wasn't living there. I didn't go to the lines. All I know was that the army of the Republika Srpska was at these positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was this something which everybody spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if you didn't see the soldiers, and if you knew that they were there, my question is, how is it you knew this? What is your source of information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: How was I to see it? I know that there was the Serbian army surrounding Sarajevo. So how could I see? Was I to go there and see with my own eyes? I knew that Sarajevo was surrounded by the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: In fact, the witness answered the question before. She was asked, "Why do you know?" She said, "Because they were shooting at us."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please move on, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document DD00-0948, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, a while ago I asked you a question and I asked you whether you remembered having had an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of October, 2002. You answered by saying no. So this is my question: After having given your statement to the OTP in 1995, which we addressed a few moments ago, do you remember having had an interview with another person from the OTP? I think this was in Sarajevo. Do you remember this? You were there with your mother.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we only have the English version on the screen, but perhaps with the help of the interpreters, who can see this on the screen, I'd like to turn to the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) You say -- perhaps I could read it out loud and this could be interpreted. "[In English] ... but states that the ABiH headquarters were some 300 metres away, but she did not see any soldiers nearby." Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "headquarters," what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: For example, on our way back from the doctor, we had to take a different road on our way back, and there was the BH army headquarters there, but there was nobody around.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, how did you know that these were the headquarters if there was nobody -- if there was nobody there? How were you able to guess this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I was able to conclude that because the headquarters was right there. But there were no soldiers to be seen. I passed the place on my way back home from the doctor, and I knew the area. I knew the place and I knew what was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But what was there exactly that would indicate that this was a headquarters of the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't understand. Can you repeat? Can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will try. You stated a few minutes ago that there were headquarters but there were no soldiers. So this is my question: How did you guess that these were headquarters? What indication was there that this would be the case? Were there weapons? Was there ammunition? Was there a flag or something of that nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: How could they possibly fly a flag there. It is was close to the Serbian positions. (redacted) (redacted) However, the road that we took on the way back was, indeed, a place where there was a BH army headquarters, but there were no weapons there. It was the civilians I had in mind who just held the place, but there were no weapons. It was just something by the roadside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: These soldiers who were headquartered there, were they perhaps protecting the neighbourhood from the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: There were those who were protecting the neighbourhood from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was there shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: How am I supposed to know? I wasn't a soldier. I was a civilian. I wasn't interested in these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us, because you are not a member of the army, are you able to tell us where the shot came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: As I said a while ago, I answered your question a while ago, didn't I? The shots came from Zecija Glava and followed us all the way to the doctors, (redacted). And also on the way back, I knew exactly where the shots were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what is your neighbourhood called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: When we were wounded or now?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The neighbourhood where you were living when this incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's another one to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now tell us, Zecija Glava, is that a mountain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Everything around Sarajevo is just hills and elevations. Yes, hills.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Does Zecija Glava belong to the same mountain -- to another mountain range, somewhat higher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I can't answer that question. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that at the time you had just moved into that neighbourhood and the incident occurred just a few days later, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: How am I supposed to know the exact day? I don't remember exactly. I can't say. I don't know how many days later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what would you say, would it be a matter of days, of weeks, of months? So when you say it was a short while afterwards, when was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I really don't know. I didn't keep track. I can't answer. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like my case manager to display the photograph which we have just seen. It's a 65 ter document, number 2990.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's the photograph we've just seen, which you should have in front of you. Do you remember that at the beginning of your testimony here we showed you a video; do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: What do you mean? A video? What video? Can you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you walked into the courtroom, we started your testimony with the examination of the Prosecution, and after a few moments you were shown a video; do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Video photograph? I remember that, the video photograph. If it's the pictures that you mean. You mean the one that I'm looking at now?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we could, first of all, display the video and perhaps move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we show this video again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, you must bring your cross-examination to a close now. You have spent for more than the time allotted without seeking an extension. I indicated that times have been allotted, and if you require an extension of the time, then you must seek it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, have I lost my right to seek this extension? Could I have an extension of the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, what do you -- how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About ten minutes, to show the witness the street map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could -- we lost, actually, the marking of the picture which is on the screen. Could the witness mark the same spot as she did earlier on? And I suggest that we record that then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honour, could I have a number for that picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We admit that as D89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I will ask my assistant to display the 65 ter number 2872, which is the street map of Sarajevo. I would like it tell the technicians that I have a problem with this computer. I cannot follow the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the matter being attended to?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. It will take a while. No, sorry, the problem has been solved as far as LiveNote is concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Your next question, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now you can see a street map of Sarajevo. Can you see where you are on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then, I would like to ask the usher to zoom in a bit, especially the right-hand part, the upper right-hand part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now read the map, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you, with the assistance of the usher, with the electronic pen, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I can only see Novo Sarajevo, Stari Grad, Alipasin Most. I can't see it, I can't find it, because the lettering is too small.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a bit more. We're talking about the right-hand part. This is the part I'm interested in. Could you please zoom in and expand it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you find your bearings now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. If we could make sure it's not broadcast again; and also, if it's tendered, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll see to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can no longer change the map, but I would like to know if you remember what was at the right-hand side of the map, which you cannot see. But if you turn the map, is it Zecija Glava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I cannot honestly tell that you because I cannot find it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That will do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have an exhibit number for this marked map. That is the place where the witness lived, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be D90.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I took her first to the place which was closest to the place where she was wounded and where the nearest doctor was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same place you showed the Prosecutor earlier on? We are talking about the same doctor, are we not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't know about the doctor. I don't know his name. That was the first time we went to see the doctor, and I really don't remember his name because I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But my question: We are talking about the same clinic, the same place where you went the day she was wounded to get first aid. You still went to the same place, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: We went to another place. After she was wounded, we went down to the road and we went to the doctor. On our way back, we took another road and returned home.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And then for the next ten days, you took the other way, the other road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: This other route between our house and the outpatient's clinic, for her wounds to be dressed. We didn't take the same route that we had taken previously when we went to fetch water.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a request for Exhibit D90. I would like it to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I wonder if you could help the Chamber identify the place where you think the shots came from. Now, I understand that you couldn't see it on the map, but is it possible that you can tell us in which direction (redacted) (redacted), where the area Zecija Glava is on the map. Is it outside the map or is it --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I can show you on the photograph. I don't understand. Are you talking about the address or the direction from which the shot came?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm talking about the place from which you believe the shots came. Can you indicate which direction from Skaljin Sokak that place was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I cannot. I cannot do that. No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Madam Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness, Mr. Sachdeva, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Can I make a very brief comment in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name, your place and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: My name is Rialda Musaefendic. I was born in Belgrade on the 4th of May, 1964.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it correct that you're currently -- is it correct that your current occupation is a programme coordinator for Sarajevo Television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, do you recall yesterday, when you met me, I showed you a statement from the 17th of May, 2006 that you gave to ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I do. You showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recall that you indicated that there were several clarifications or amendments you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask that 65 ter 02994 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the front page of the statement there on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see on the bottom of the first page your signature, at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. On the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to paragraph 4 on the English and on the B/C/S versions. If you look carefully at paragraph 4, there is a sentence that starts: "I later learned that the bomb landed on the gravel on the roof of the second floor where it exploded, and pieces of the bomb and debris were able to later be seen in the area of the atrium between the buildings." Do you see that written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is there an amendment or a clarification you would like to make to this sentence; and if there is, please explain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Not in this sentence but in the next sentence, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Please explain the amendment, then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: In this statement it says that later I learned that the bomb landed on the second floor, where it exploded, and pieces of the bomb and debris were able to later be seen in the area between the buildings. I don't believe this is true. The bomb did not explode on the roof; it actually hit it and it exploded in the atrium, more precisely where studio C was. So it first impacted - how shall I put it? - and after that slid, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now I take you to paragraph 7. In paragraph 7, do you see where it says: "Another employee, Margaret, was next to me and I remember her calling my name and trying to help me stand up." Do you see that written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is there a clarification or an amendment you'd like to make to this sentence; and if there is, please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I would like to amend it, although everything, what it says here, is correct. I was pushed by the detonation and covered with debris. My colleague Margaret was in the office across the hall. Everything was in rubble, but she ran to me, dug me out, so to speak, and helped me get out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can you look at paragraph 12. In paragraph 12, the sentence that starts: "I also had a piece of shrapnel embedded in my right cheek." Do you see that sentence there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And same question: Is there an amendment or a clarification that you would like to make to that; and, in so, please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to make a clarification to this. It is right that I had cuts above both eyes and the surface of my skin was damaged by shards and things. But it's not very clear to me, this piece of shrapnel, if it is a piece of the bomb, I wouldn't be sitting here alive. In the next sentence it is better explained. It was just pieces of glass and reinforced concrete and thick walls and windows, which means that the detonation has pushed all the windows out, destroyed everything in the offices. And all these pieces of debris flying around were embedded into the bodies of all the people who were sitting in their offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And lastly can I take you to paragraph -- well, we'll have to go to the next page, and if you could focus on paragraph 23, please. In paragraph 23, where you speak about the problems with bread, there is a sentence that starts: "So I went with another driver and we attempted to distribute some bread." Do you see that sentence there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you wish to make a clarification or amendment to that sentence; and if so, please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, there is one thing I'd like to clarify. The greatest problem was bread. Simply, there was no flour, water, or electricity in Sarajevo. If there was any to be had, it was only in very small quantities. The principal bakery in Sarajevo had limited quantities of bread. However, simply because many people had been killed on account of the frequent shelling -- the old name of the square was Pero Kosoric Square, which was now called the Hero's Square, which is where I lived during the war. Drivers were often killed there. In the meantime, in our neighbourhood, many refugees from Grbavica had arrived and there wasn't enough bread for everyone. All I'm trying to say here is that I was not a driver myself. I was a civilian, and it was at my own initiative that I headed for the bakery just in order to get some bread for my own family. I'm not sure if that is sufficiently clear, or should I elaborate?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, that's fine. The clarification is that you were not the driver; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, given these clarifications and amendments that you've made here in court, does this statement now accurately reflect what happened on the 28th of June, 1995, and also the experiences you had during the conflict, with those clarifications made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Given the fact that the number of pages is not that extensive, it's true, what you say. It's all true, in fact, but a lot of additions could still be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, very well. I will go through a few questions to elicit further evidence on some issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. President, Your Honours, I would like to tender this statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Musaefendic, you spoke just briefly about the injury that you sustained to your cheek during this incident, and I want to ask you: Did you go to hospital after that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: All of those who were injured were instantly taken to the Kosevo Hospital and we received medical assistance, depending on our injuries and under the circumstances that prevailed. All of us were assisted, and so was I. The greatest problem for me was my eyes, because I wasn't able to see. I wasn't able to use either of my eyes because of the blood, because of the pieces of metal, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to bring up 65 ter 00185A.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a document on your screen there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I see the B/C/S on the right-hand side and what I assume to be the translation on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is this document, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I assume that this is one of those documents from the hospital, the ones I got from being admitted. Upon arriving on the 28th of June at the Kosevo Hospital, I was treated immediately. And after that -- I had bandages over both my eyes. And after that, I would go regularly. Since there were a lot more people at the hospital that sustained more serious injuries than mine, I would come on a daily basis to receive injections to both my eyes because the pressure in my eyes was very high. And I think it's one of those doctors - what should I call them? - the Czechs. I'm sorry if I'm being too effusive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, if you could try and keep your answers as brief as possible because we are under a time-limit. So what I want to ask you now is: With this doctor's record, do the injuries indicated on the record conform to the injuries you sustained from that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for your information, for Your Honours' information, this record has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, let's talk very briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: With which P number; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be of assistance to the Chamber. 65 ter 00185, page 39, that is the e-court reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, okay, I want to talk -- ask you a few questions about the incident at the TV building. Firstly, what time did you go into work that morning, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I remember because it was a special day for me; it was my mother's birthday. It was at about 7.00 in the morning. I got up early and walked to the TV building. I was expecting a colleague of mine to fetch some food for our team, from Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Again, if you could keep your answers as succinct as possible, that would be most appreciated. So you got to the building at 7.00 in the morning. What time, do you remember, did the explosion occur, if you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I arrived at about 7.30. Half an hour is what I normally take to walk to work. The explosion occurred at about 10 or 20 minutes past 9.00. It's difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And during that time, from 7.30 until 20 minutes past 9.00, were you at the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. In the office, the office which was in the TV building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: During that time that you were there, did you notice or see any heavy weaponry or mortar weapons belonging to the Bosnian government forces in the building or in and around the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Throughout that time and during the arrival itself, not in the building or around the building. I did not see any of the weapons that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you see during that time any military personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, I did not see any military personnel. Just the usual TV building security, people who are Sarajevo TV's employees, janitors. I'm not sure what I should call them. Security men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: After the explosion, did you find out or did you know if anyone was killed as a result of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: It was in the hospital that we were told that one person had been killed and many had been wounded, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: As you -- after the explosion, as you left the building, did you notice any bodies on the ground, in the building or near the building at all, while you were leaving the office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: After the explosion, some of our colleagues were taking those of us who had been wounded or injured through the main entrance of the TV building; the only entrance, for that matter. Outside the building itself there were a great many wounded. I saw a body lying to the right, as you leave the building. There was a man on the ground. Of course people were trying to help. At this point in time I didn't know if any of them were dead. Everybody was just trying to reach the hospital as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you say you saw a body lying to the right as you leave the building; there was a man on the ground. Are you saying that the body lying to the right was the man on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: It wasn't just he. There were people around him, helping, and there were other colleagues who were wounded and they were standing. It was a messy scene. I'm not sure how I should put it. At this point in time I didn't know who was alive and who was dead. There were people there who were still alive as well, who were helping each other. I'm not sure how I should explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, maybe my question is not concise enough. I'm just trying to get a connection. The body you saw lying to the right, is that the man that you say was on the ground? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were at the office, from 7.30 up until the explosion, did you notice anyone bringing in bodies or a body to the atrium or the office, at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: At the time I was inside the office - so I wasn't outside the office - I was in no position to see or hear anything. I was inside the office at that point in time and that was on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How many people were working at the office at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I think about 12 persons. Twelve.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If a dead body had been brought in prior to the explosion, would that have been noticed by your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Frankly, that would have been impossible. It would have been impossible to do something like that for a very simple reason: This is an official building, a state institution, and it's impossible to get past security. Zillions of journalists, both foreign and domestic, it's impossible to get something like this past them without anybody noticing, something that just wasn't right; like a dead body, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And you earlier mentioned that you left through the only exit of the building after the explosion. If somebody had brought a body in at that time, would that have been noticed or witnessed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, when you met me yesterday, do you remember giving me two DVDs with -- well, do you remember giving me two DVDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I do. I remember clearly giving you two DVDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What were on those DVDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: On one of those, there's the ARD TV coverage, and in the other DVD, there's some old material with a coverage by Bosnia-Herzegovina TV as well see CNN and SkyNews coverage, at least to the extent that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The ARD TV coverage, well, firstly, can you say, which news company is that, and where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: As far as I know, this is a German, state-owned TV station. I'm not sure exactly how you spell that in German, but I think it's ARD. It's quite well known, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's okay. Thank you. Who gave you this -- well, who gave you these DVDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: The ARD DVD is one that I'd asked a copy of, this footage from the war, a war story, when I was wounded, and Mladen Pehar, who was a cameraman for ARD at the time, provided a copy to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mladen Pehar, where did he work at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: For ARD. And he was Sarajevo-based.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And where was his office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: On the second floor, same corridor as mine. Two doors down the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That is the TV building in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The TV building, second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to concentrate on the DVD you gave me from the ARD, the German television -- the German news company. What is on that DVD?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: At the time Mladen Pehar was cleaning his camera, getting it ready for new footage, for that day's footage, as any cameraman would do first thing in the morning. This is something I learned later on. So you can hear and see the sound of an explosion and the whole works; the dreadful site of the offices in the corridor that had just been destroyed, people wounded, the very first seconds following the explosion. He hadn't realised himself that he had filmed it. It was only later on, when he put the whole thing together for another journalist, that he realised that he even got -- those early moments after the blast had also been filmed. So that's the first DVD. And in case you should require more information, I can provide further details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, if I require, I'll ask you. I just want to be clear, although I think it is it clear, but you say at the time Mladen Pehar was cleaning his camera and getting it ready for new footage. When you say "at that time," is it your evidence that it was five or ten minutes prior to 9.20 or prior to the explosion at the TV building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: At the time I wasn't in Mladen Pehar's office. However, as any cameraman worth his salt would do, before he started filming, he had prepared his kit, his camera. He would get it all ready for the actual filming. And I'm sure that he had spent the five or ten minutes just before 9.00 doing that, because 9.00 is when everybody starts work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to play an excerpt from that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sachdeva, before moving on to this, the witness has just talked about the explosion. I would like, Witness, to ask you the following question: You said that you heard some noise in relation to this incident, so I would like to know the following: What kind of noise did you hear? Was it the sound coming from an engine, from some flying object, or was it the sound of a blast or of the explosion which we just talked about, which was filmed and which we will be able to see in the video in a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, it's very difficult to keep it brief. The first sound I heard was a very powerful impact. I never heard a sound like that before. I had heard shells exploding, mortars, snipers, that sort of thing, but nothing like that. When the impact occurred, everyone in the office was dead scared and we all threw ourselves down on the floor in order to take cover, in a way. This sound was followed by an even stranger sound. The best description that I could come up with is a thousand tiny feet walking on pebbles. It's a very curious sound that I will never forget. So it wasn't before the flashes started, these strange flashes. A huge flash and then the detonation and then the ensuing chaos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you a literary person? I was asking if you are a literary person. I rather liked your description of "a thousand tiny feet walking on pebbles."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not a literary person. I'm just telling you the story straight from the heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Before I get to the excerpt, can I just ask, Mrs. Musaefendic, are you depicted in this first DVD? Did you see yourself in that DVD after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I may now instruct my case manager to start the DVD, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: You anticipated my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the ARD office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, this is not the TV building, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No. This is a residential building in Sarajevo, at Alipasa's. It's a neighbourhood in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the bodies that we just saw being brought out on a stretcher just before this clip do not relate to the TV building incident, do they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No, they don't. They relate to this building, tenants from this building. That's what crews usually filmed, human suffering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could just finish the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mrs. Musaefendic, does this excerpt -- is this excerpt an accurate recording of news footage that you received from your colleague Mladen Pehar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move to tender this excerpt into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is the chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm Defence counsel for Dragomir Milosevic, and I would like you to give me certain answers, if possible, and please keep it brief. I would begin with a few questions relating to what you have already been asked by my learned colleague Mr. Sachdeva. Can you tell me, please, after how much time when you heard this object sliding into the building did the explosion occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by "sliding."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you first heard an impact on the roof.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How many seconds after that did you hear the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I didn't measure it. It seemed to me a long time, but it wasn't, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Secondly, the man who was lying on the ground when you were leaving the building and the people surrounding him, at that point in time you didn't know what had happened to this man.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Excuse me, this man was not alone. There were many people from the TV building who were injured there as well. This is where there's a kind of roof above the entrance and people were standing there, waiting for vehicles to take them to hospital. And as I said, at that moment I myself didn't know how many people were injured or whether there were any dead people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: No. I was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, so you were taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know at all what happened subsequently? Was anyone taken into the atrium after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me be more precise. Do you know at all what happened subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: What happened later I don't know, because at that time I was in the hospital and I personally didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't know if anyone was subsequently taken into the atrium of the TV building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Since this was a TV building, there were lots of cameramen there, filming. As far as I was able to see, there was no one being carried into -- inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this video that we have just seen, or part thereof, these two DVDs were given to the Defence only yesterday. I do not object to that. I managed to review part of this material. And I would now ask my case manager to show two things from these same DVDs but they relate to Mr. Silajdzic's statement given on that day and the statement given by the representative of UNPROFOR on the scene. And, if possible, I would like this to be translated for you, or, rather, for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is it that we just saw, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just saw part of the same video, the fraction of which was shown by Mr. Sachdeva. However, I decided to show something that I believe you should hear, so it's the same CD and I move for it entirely to be entered into evidence, not just the excerpt that we saw, but including these two statements. And these should be admitted as counsel exhibits, and this material should not be shown in -- in portions but, rather, as a whole. And, therefore, I move for it to be tendered into evidence as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just be reminded to as what it is that we have already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That was excerpt taken from the DVD; in other words, yes, an excerpt from the entirety of the DVD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And this is another excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: This is from that same DVD; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To be admitted under a separate number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it and give it a different number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D91, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Witness, can you tell me at that time when this incident happened, which truly is a horrible one, were there fierce clashes between the warring parties at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Was there a conflict between two warring parties, is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: As far as I know that was an aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina. There were no two warring parties. Because there were on one side ordinary people without arms; and on the other side, there was an armed force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I understand. In those days was there shooting from both sides and even more from the people in Sarajevo who, according to you, were defending themselves or then from the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, on that particular morning, sniping activity was something habitual on my way from my house to work. However, that was customary, but on that particular day it was rather quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to this. Now, I have in front of me the statement date 17th of May, 2006, already tendered by the Prosecution. But there is another statement, too, given on the 28th of June, 1995, or rather, on the 19th of July, and it refers to the incident of the 26th of June, and it was given to the Security Services of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. If you show to me and I see my signature, I will remember. I know that I gave a statement to the Security Services and investigators of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but I honestly don't remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Besides, you gave another statement to the ICTY investigators on the 11th of March, 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I remember giving a statement both to the ICTY investigators and the Sarajevo police, but I can't recall the dates until unless you show the documents to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask, first, for your statement given on the 19th of July, 1995 given to the Security Services of Sarajevo, which is 65 ter number 00185, e-court page 85, 00873890. You can see this statement. I'm not going to read it to you in its entirety. In the preamble, you can see that at the time you were employed as a traffic technician with a WTN company, which is an American company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge this because the letters are too small, and I can't read it properly. Yes, now I can see clearly. It says in Bosnian that I was a transport technician and that is what my qualification was, and it is true that I was working for the American WTN agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd rather not read the whole statement, but if it is necessary we may well do so. But, look, you say here that this happened at 10 past 9.00. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me read it for you. "About 10 past 9.00, I heard an unnatural sound that I had not heard until by then, and it was followed by a heavy thump. At that moment, I ducked and squatted down covering my head with my hand." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. First an impact and then a strange sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then you go on to say: "During the next seven or eight seconds nothing happened, so I stood up and looked in the direction of the window."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did it -- was it really seven or eight seconds that elapsed? Do you know how long that is it before the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: Yes. I know how long seven or eight seconds are, and I'm sorry I really don't see the point of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you abide by your statement that seven or eight seconds elapsed before you heard the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember how much time elapsed. Just like I told you a minute ago, it seemed to be a long time. It may have been shorter, but I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to press this matter any further. I have my own ideas about this, but it's not up to me to comment. Further on in the document, you say --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please indicate where the sentence starts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, where does the sentence begin, And remember we don't have a translation in English. We now have the English. Where does the sentence begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It begins, "At that moment I heard a strong impact and then an unnatural flare. I heard another detonation and then silence followed, because I lost consciousness as a result of shock that I had endured."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-50
